articles.originalTitle: Ai Weiwei unveils his epic new Australian work: ‘90% of art is just garbage. Real art questions the existing order’ - The Guardian
articles.title: Ai Weiwei Unveils Epic Combat Helmet Sculpture on Sydney Harbour
articles.excerpt: Artist Ai Weiwei has unveiled a 40-metre-long installation outside Sydney's Museum of Contemporary Art, reflecting on the destructive mechanics of modern warfare and the fragility of life.
articles.content: Living at his farm in Portugal, renowned artist Ai Weiwei has introduced his latest installation, Mushrooms, on the Tallawoladah Lawn outside the Museum of Contemporary Art on Sydney Harbour. Spanning 40 metres, the monumental installation features 500 identical cast iron sculptures shaped like combat helmets arranged on an elevated platform. The title references both the visual similarities between mushroom caps and military helmets, and the associations with decay, death, and life's fragility exposed by armed conflict. The artist noted that the project's origins connect to his 2015 documentary on the migrant crisis and his subsequent studies of military arsenals and modern warfare mechanics. Having visited frontline Ukrainian soldiers last year, Ai chose the location—overlooking the Sydney Opera House—to reiterate that peace remains essential for civilised society. Critiquing contemporary institutional art as largely decorative and detached from human struggle, Ai maintains that genuine art must challenge existing orders and judgments. The installation is currently open to the public.

articles.originalTitle: Herzog & de Meuron reuses foundations for mass-timber Massachusetts school building - Dezeen
articles.title: Herzog and de Meuron Reuses Foundations for Massachusetts School Building
articles.excerpt: Swiss studio Herzog and de Meuron utilized the existing concrete foundation of an older 1960s structure for the new Student Center and Dining Commons at Amherst College, adding mass-timber levels on top.
articles.content: Swiss architecture studio Herzog and de Meuron has completed the Student Center and Dining Commons at Amherst College in Massachusetts. The project utilizes the existing concrete foundations and skeleton of the 1960s Merrill Science Center, a brutalist brick building originally designed by Boston firm Campbell, Aldrich and Nulty. The studio chose to retain the preexisting foundations to navigate the sloped site and support the college's carbon neutrality goals. The building was expanded from 7,432 to 11,148 square meters to house a combined student center and dining hall. Mass-timber structural columns derived from Canadian Black Spruce were attached to the concrete columns on the second level, while the third and fourth levels are constructed almost entirely from mass timber. The upper floors feature Western Red Cedar cladding, whereas the lower levels utilize a dark-toned cedar finish. Solar panels were installed on fourth-level pavilions to aid energy efficiency. The architecture studio reported a 33 percent reduction in embodied carbon and a 93 percent reduction in operational carbon compared to similar building types. This project marks the studio's first completed educational building in the United States.

articles.originalTitle: Architectural Details: Snider House Bridges Past and Present - Architizer
articles.title: Giannone Petricone Associates Revitalizes 1828 Snider House in North Toronto
articles.excerpt: Giannone Petricone Associates has restored and updated Snider House, North Toronto's oldest surviving building, blending historic design with a glass addition.
articles.content: Giannone Petricone Associates has restored and revitalized Snider House, identified as the oldest surviving building in North Toronto. Originally built in 1828 in the Regency style, the landmark was upgraded to modern standards while preserving its historic character. The original Regency cottage façade maintains its formal, symmetrical presence at the front, while a contemporary rear glass extension opens the dwelling to the landscape. Co-founding principal Pina Petricone notes that the firm approaches heritage projects to celebrate distinct attributes through contrast and layering. The standout architectural feature at the rear is an undulating, two-story glass façade. Fabricated using a gravity-curved method on hot sand beds in Spain and combined with low-E insulated glass technology, this custom curtain wall contrasts with the heavy clay brick of the original structure. Inside, the restored interior balances heritage formality with material restraint, maintaining warmth in the dining and sitting rooms. The kitchen and adjoining living areas open fully to the backyard. Reimagined wide baseboards function simultaneously as visual accents and air diffusers, helping the historic home meet contemporary standards.

articles.originalTitle: Painting believed to be a newly discovered Goya to go on show at Museo del Prado in 2028 - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: Painting Believed to Be by Goya Slated for 2028 Exhibition at Museo del Prado
articles.excerpt: Spain's culture ministry and Madrid's Museo del Prado are operating under the assumption that a painting owned by gallerist Artur Ramon is an unknown work by Francisco de Goya, slated for a 2028 exhibition.
articles.content: Spain's culture ministry and Madrid's Museo del Prado indicated that a painting owned by gallerist Artur Ramon appears to be an unknown work by Francisco de Goya. Purchased at a Madrid auction in 2018, El milagro de la aparición del eucaristo al San Pascual Bailón was previously attributed to Francisco Bayeu, Goya's brother-in-law. During the pandemic lockdown, Ramon began questioning the attribution based on stylistic traits in the anatomy and use of light. After his export application for the work was denied, the ministry stated that, pending in-depth study, indicators suggest the piece is an unknown Goya from around 1780. The Museo del Prado confirmed the painting will be included in a 2028 exhibition commemorating the 200th anniversary of the artist's death, providing an opportunity for a formal investigation to confirm its authorship. Prior to the Prado exhibition, the work will be shown at the Artur Ramon Gallery in October.

articles.originalTitle: Fondation Beyeler Expands with Three New Buildings by Peter Zumthor - ArchDaily
articles.title: Fondation Beyeler Expands with Three New Buildings by Peter Zumthor
articles.excerpt: Fondation Beyeler in Riehen, Switzerland, is expanding its museum ensemble with three new buildings designed by architect Peter Zumthor, an enlarged park, and the adaptive reuse of historic structures.
articles.content: Fondation Beyeler in Riehen, Switzerland, is expanding its museum ensemble with three new buildings designed by Swiss architect Peter Zumthor, alongside an enlarged park and restored historic structures. The expansion adds to the existing museum designed by Renzo Piano, incorporating the Wyss Museum, the Ammann Pavilion, and the Erlen Torhaus. The three-storey Wyss Museum provides approximately 1,500 square meters of exhibition space using locally quarried Jura limestone. The single-storey Ammann Pavilion functions as a public lounge during the day and hosts cultural events in the evening, while the Erlen Torhaus contains artwork handling facilities and workspaces. The project nearly doubles the size of Beyeler Park by adding nearly 10,000 square meters of formerly private parkland, retaining mature trees and integrating new meadows and artworks. Furthermore, several historic structures including the Orangerie, Ammann Atelier, Salon, and Folly were adapted for art education, music, botany, and experimental projects. The expanded campus begins welcoming visitors following a preview phase.

articles.originalTitle: Derrick Adams, Randy Polumbo, Wills Glasspiegel & More Artists Project Newly-Commissioned Works Onto Historic Hangars in Brooklyn - Hyperallergic
articles.title: Historic New York Hangars to Host Public Arts Projection Festival
articles.excerpt: The Floyd Bennett Field Public Arts Festival will transform NYC's first airport with large-scale projection mapping across historic airplane hangar facades.
articles.content: New York City's first airport, Floyd Bennett Field, is preparing to host a public arts festival celebrating community and the Jamaica Bay landscape. The event will feature 15 new artworks projection-mapped onto the 8,640-square-foot facades of two historic airplane hangars. Participating artists including Derrick Adams, Randy Polumbo, Wills Glasspiegel, LaJuné McMillian, and Ryan Hartley Smith will present works centered on themes of water, nature, and innovation. The installations explore the site's waterfront connection near the Atlantic Ocean, creating a dynamic interplay between past and present as the historic buildings undergo revitalization. For one evening, the art-deco architecture will be animated through light, movement, and digital storytelling. Open to all visitors, the outdoor festival offers an opportunity to experience large-scale projection mapping alongside live music within the park environment.

articles.originalTitle: About the Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires exhibition - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: V&A Exhibition Explores 1,600 Years of Imperial Legacy in Constantinople and Istanbul
articles.excerpt: The Victoria and Albert Museum is launching the Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires exhibition on November 7, 2026, exploring 1,600 years of artistic production from AD 330 to 1922.
articles.content: V&A South Kensington in London is preparing to open a major exhibition examining 1,600 years of artistic production spanning the Byzantine and Ottoman empires. Opening on November 7, 2026, the exhibition titled Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires explores the enduring creative legacy of an imperial capital that shaped the Mediterranean world between AD 330 and 1922. Tracing the distinct yet connected traditions of both successive empires, the showcase brings together over 200 objects, including rare textiles, ceramic tiles, mosaics, precious metalwork, sculpture, manuscripts, and paintings. Structured across four main sections titled Grand Beginnings, Heaven and Earth, Power and Reach, and Life in the City, the exhibition illustrates themes ranging from imperial identity and patronage to the rhythms of urban life. The display concludes by highlighting the influence of Byzantine and Ottoman art on 19th-century Europe through works from the V&A collection.

articles.originalTitle: peter zumthor's expanded fondation beyeler opens to the public - Designboom
articles.title: Peter Zumthor's Expanded Fondation Beyeler Opens to the Public
articles.excerpt: Peter Zumthor's expansion of the Fondation Beyeler in Riehen near Basel is opening to the public gradually. Three new buildings, an expanded park, and restored historic structures extend the museum grounds.
articles.content: Peter Zumthor's expansion of the Fondation Beyeler in Riehen near Basel begins its opening to the public with a gradual rollout starting September 26, 2026, ahead of a full opening in January 2027. The project extends Renzo Piano's existing structure with three new buildings, an expanded park, and restored historic structures. Zumthor distributed the expansion's functions across the Wyss Museum, Ammann Pavilion, and Erlen Torhaus to avoid a single oversized volume. The Wyss Museum adds roughly 1,500 square meters of exhibition space and features Jura limestone alongside a hand-built rammed-concrete facade. The single-story glass and oak Ammann Pavilion functions as a public lounge during the day and a cultural events venue in the evening. Additionally, the project opens nearly 10,000 square meters of formerly private parkland to visitors, connecting the gardens directly to the nearby nature reserve.

articles.originalTitle: Google Unveils New Renderings of Chicago's Thompson Center Redesign, Marking Its Escape From Demolition - ArchDaily
articles.title: Chicago's Thompson Center Escapes Demolition with New Redesign Renderings
articles.excerpt: Chicago's postmodern James R. Thompson Center is being redeveloped as a space for work, culture, and community, escaping demolition through a collaboration with studio A+I.
articles.content: New redevelopment renderings have been released for the James R. Thompson Center in Chicago's Loop, designed by Helmut Jahn and completed in 1985. Commissioned by Governor James R. Thompson, the postmodern building features a multicolored glass atrium and a sloping corner entry. Facing criticism over maintenance costs and climate control issues, the structure was repeatedly threatened with demolition until preservationists campaigned for its protection. The building was sold to The Prime Group in 2022, and Google announced plans to purchase it following renovations. Renovations began in May 2024, involving the removal of portions of the original exterior and atrium. Developed in collaboration with Architecture Plus Information, now part of Perkins&Will, the redesign integrates food, retail, and seasonal event spaces into the 17-story atrium and plaza. The revamped public area will also house Vector, a 30-foot sculpture by artist Sanford Biggers, alongside a large-scale commissioned piece produced with the local nonprofit After School Matters.

articles.originalTitle: Standout Collectible Designs at Paris Design Week 2026 - WWD
articles.title: Standout Collectible Designs Unveiled During Paris Design Week 2026
articles.excerpt: The 16th edition of Paris Design Week showcased contemporary designs and decor rooted in traditional techniques and natural forms across the city.
articles.content: Paris Design Week brought together contemporary design works across showrooms in Saint-Germain-des-Prés and beyond with the participation of 500 exhibitors. During the event, Draga & Aurel showcased their Crisalide side tables combining colored glass and brass bases at Galerie BSL. Pinto partnered with fabric firm Nobilis to present the Foundation collection in warm tones. Yves Salomon Éditions unveiled Tactile Monuments, its first complete interior collection inspired by natural stone forms. Swedish design house Veermakers opened its first Paris showroom in Le Marais, highlighting Scandinavian cabinetmaking traditions. Nordic Knots presented hand-knotted wool rugs inspired by the Swedish Grace movement, while L’Objet and jeweler Jessica McCormack debuted a marine-themed home collection. Modern Metier presented the Tropic of Capricorn collection created with French designer Rudy Guénaire. Garnier & Linker introduced the Aurora outdoor lighting series, and Franck Genser presented his Piscine VI collection. Hervet Manufacturier showcased its first full range building on six generations of woodworking expertise.

articles.originalTitle: Art Institute of Chicago restitutes Metzinger painting sold in Nazi-occupied Amsterdam - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: Art Institute of Chicago to restitute Metzinger painting sold under Nazi persecution
articles.excerpt: The Art Institute of Chicago has agreed to return a 1913 Jean Metzinger painting to the heirs of Jewish art collector Emanuel Lewenstein, concluding that the artwork was sold as a result of Nazi persecution in occupied Amsterdam.
articles.content: The Art Institute of Chicago agreed to restitute a painting by Jean Metzinger to the heirs of Jewish art collector Emanuel Lewenstein. The 1913 work, titled Woman With a Fan, was auctioned in October 1940 in Amsterdam following the Nazi invasion. According to the museum's head of provenance research, Jacques Schuhmacher, the sale was treated as a forced transaction resulting from Nazi persecution. Researchers used infrared photography to uncover faint pencil markings on the reverse of the canvas, identifying dealer Paul Citroen and linking the piece to the Lewenstein family. Stuart Eizenstat, a United States official who shaped the 1998 Washington Principles, praised the cooperation between the museum and the heirs. Another piece from the 1940 Amsterdam sale, a Wassily Kandinsky painting, is slated for a London auction where it is expected to draw significant attention, while the family continues to search for roughly 100 missing works. In an unrelated legal matter, a New York appeals court ruled that investigators exceeded their authority when seizing an Egon Schiele drawing from the museum using criminal penal codes.

articles.originalTitle: Meet the Young Practices Shaping Architecture’s Next Chapter - Architizer
articles.title: Architizer Announces Winners of the 14th Annual A+Awards Best Young Firm
articles.excerpt: The winners of Architizer's 14th Annual A+Awards Best Young Firm category have been announced, highlighting emerging studios from diverse backgrounds that test the boundaries of architecture across climate, culture, and materials.
articles.content: The jury and public have selected the winners of Architizer's 14th Annual A+Awards, showcasing emerging practices that offer a glimpse into the future of the discipline. Jakarta-based RAD+ar won the jury prize for Best Young Firm through tropical architecture projects like Aruma Split Garden and Hidden Garden House. K-Thengono Design Studio received the popular choice award, utilizing vernacular methods and natural materials in Indonesia. Founded in Hong Kong and Shanghai, SKYnoa focuses on retail concepts blending Spanish, German, and Chinese perspectives. Toronto's PHAEDRUS Studio treats design as an open-ended dialogue across architecture and interiors. Shanghai-based EERI explores everyday essentials through multidisciplinary installations and architectural scales. Beijing Ger Architecture Technology specializes in prefabricated construction for rural revitalization and grassland communities in China. Chicago-based interior design studio Crespo & Br. centers its growing portfolio on hospitality projects. Finally, St. Louis practice AVV A integrates computational design, digital fabrication, and AI with traditional craft for cultural and public projects.

articles.originalTitle: Sansetsukon x Es Devlin: MILK - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: Dance Collective Sansetsukon Performs New Live Work at V&A East Storehouse
articles.excerpt: Dance collective Sansetsukon is staging MILK, a new live performance responding to Es Devlin's installation The Everythingists, at the V&A East Storehouse.
articles.content: Dance collective Sansetsukon is presenting MILK, a new live performance responding to Es Devlin's installation The Everythingists through dance, sound, light, and shadow. Staged as a free special event on 3 October 2026 at the V&A East Storehouse, the performance creates a dialogue between the dancers, the installation, and the surrounding gallery space. The work draws inspiration from Rayonism and the concept of new art challenging old art, while also exploring ideas of humans empowered by machines and machines empowered by individuals. Set to an audio soundscape created by reworking material from The Everythingists, the 25 to 30-minute performance takes place across three sessions. The production features dancers including Joshua Shanny-Wynter, Deavion Brown, and Robbie Ordoña, alongside a creative team comprising composer Serian Griffiths and lighting designer Oliver Pritchard.

articles.originalTitle: 200,000 young people and counting: Tate celebrates a new generation with landmark commission for young artists - tate.org.uk
articles.title: Tate Collective Reaches 200,000 Members and Launches Landmark Commission for Young Artists
articles.excerpt: Tate Collective, a free membership scheme for 16-to-25-year-olds, has reached 200,000 members as Tate Modern launches an open call for a young artist's work to be displayed in the gallery.
articles.content: Tate’s free membership scheme for 16-to-25-year-olds, Tate Collective, has reached a milestone of 200,000 members. To mark the occasion, Tate Modern has launched a landmark open call inviting members to create a new artwork for display within the gallery alongside renowned figures such as Andy Warhol, Salvador Dalí, and Marina Abramović. Entries for the commission remain open until October 19, with the winning work selected by a jury chaired by Rosalie Doubal for display at Tate Modern in March 2027. Concurrently, Tate Modern Lates is celebrating its 10th anniversary, having welcomed 870,000 attendees over the past decade. The celebrations will culminate on Friday, October 30, with a special anniversary event featuring programming by multidisciplinary artist Shygirl. Interim Director Karin Hindsbo noted that the initiatives aim to empower young people to participate in culture as active contributors and creators shaping the future of art.

articles.originalTitle: Biennale College Architettura 2026/2027: the 12 selected projects - labiennale.org
articles.title: Twelve Projects Selected for Biennale College Architettura 2026-2027
articles.excerpt: Twelve projects have been selected for the third edition of Biennale College Architettura. The projects by practitioners under 30 will be developed during a workshop from 22 to 30 September 2026.
articles.content: Twelve projects have been selected for the 3rd edition of Biennale College Architettura 2026–2027. The emerging practitioners under 30 originate from China, Croatia, Italy, Mexico, Syria, Spain, Turkey, Tunisia, the USA, and Hungary. The initiative complements the 20th International Architecture Exhibition, titled Do Architecture and curated by Wang Shu and Lu Wenyu, serving as a research, experimentation, and production laboratory. The open call attracted over 80 emerging practitioners from 36 countries. The 12 selected projects are presented by Ahlem Balghouthi, Fabio Bari, Stav Bouzaglo, Antonino Caridi, Yiying Chen, Alejandro Ferrer Esplugues, Jin Gao, Nisa Gökgöz, Matej Orkić, Julia Polefko, Ahmad Salah, and Guillermo Sanchez Cardenas. The workshop will take place from 22 to 30 September 2026, coordinated by Wang Shu and Lu Wenyu alongside tutors. Following the workshop, up to four projects will be selected to receive a 25,000 euro grant for the realization of the final work, which will be presented out of competition during Biennale Architettura 2027.

articles.originalTitle: Art Basel Paris 2026 Press Dossier: a deep-dive into this year's highlights - Art Basel
articles.title: Art Basel Paris 2026 Opens with 211 Galleries and Expanded Public Programming
articles.excerpt: Hosting 211 galleries from 41 countries and regions, Art Basel Paris returns this autumn with an expanded public program concentrated around the Grand Palais and numerous first-time participants.
articles.content: Set to open in September, Art Basel Paris prepares to welcome 211 galleries, including 183 in Galeries, 16 in Emergence, and 12 in Premise. Featuring participants from 41 countries and regions, the fair features the relocation of Premise to a larger space alongside conversations hosted in the Salon Seine and the Grand Palais Auditorium. Thirty-two galleries are participating for the first time, while 64 galleries operating in France maintain a central role. Entities such as Petrine and The Pill transition from Emergence into the main Galeries sector, alongside the continued strong presence of established international art dealers. Reflecting the plural artistic landscape of the Parisian scene, presentations bring together painting, installation, performance, literature, and moving images. The program pairs works by artists born or based in Paris with broader international practices across curated booths. The fair opens with the Avant-Première preview scheduled for October 20.

articles.originalTitle: ARTIST ROOMS: Robert Rauschenberg at Tate Modern, 21 September 2026 - December 2027 – Press Release - tate.org.uk
articles.title: Tate Modern Opens Large-Scale Robert Rauschenberg Display
articles.excerpt: Tate Modern is launching a large-scale free display of over 20 works by Robert Rauschenberg spanning three decades to mark the centenary of his birth.
articles.content: Tate Modern is launching a large-scale free display of works by Robert Rauschenberg, running from 21 September 2026 to December 2027. Marking the centenary of the artist's birth, the presentation brings together over 20 works spanning three decades, including paintings, prints, and kinetic installations. At the heart of the presentation are Glut sculptures, including three newly gifted by the Robert Rauschenberg Foundation to the Tate Americas Foundation. Curated by Gregor Muir, Andrew de Brún, and Julia Blaut, the display foregrounds Rauschenberg's engagement with dance and performance, featuring metal sculptures, performance sets, and costume designs. The exhibition is organized as part of the ARTIST ROOMS touring programme, jointly managed by Tate and the National Galleries of Scotland.

articles.originalTitle: Glenn Brown in: Fail We May, Sail We Must | Museum Exhibitions | News - Gagosian
articles.title: Brown Collection in London Opens New Exhibition
articles.excerpt: Curated by Glenn Brown and Edgar Laguinia, the exhibition brings together works by more than twenty artists.
articles.content: The Brown Collection in London has announced its upcoming exhibition titled Fail We May, Sail We Must. Scheduled to run from September 25, 2026, to August 7, 2027, the presentation is curated by Glenn Brown and Brown Collection cofounder Edgar Laguinia. The selection features historic and contemporary paintings, sculptures, drawings, prints, and ceramics spanning six centuries by more than twenty artists. Incorporating spliced collages, double images, and elongated figures with elements of playfulness and humor, the exhibition aims to establish new connections between works not commonly seen together. Separately, the latest issue of Gagosian Quarterly highlights works, conversations, and projects by Brice Marden, Jordan Wolfson, Cady Noland, Tyler Mitchell, Adriana Varejão, and Jennifer Guidi. Among the features, Adriana Varejão discusses her working practice in preparation for representing Brazil at the 61st Biennale di Venezia.

articles.originalTitle: Maison Michel Celebrates 90 Years of Hatmaking With New Exhibition at Chanel’s Le19M - WWD
articles.title: Maison Michel Celebrates 90th Anniversary With New Exhibition at Chanel Hub
articles.excerpt: Famed Parisian hatmaker Maison Michel is marking its 90th anniversary with a comprehensive exhibition opening at Chanel’s craftsmanship hub, Le19M, in northern Paris.
articles.content: Paris-based hatmaker Maison Michel is marking its 90th anniversary with an exhibition titled "Metamorphoses — The Hats of Maison Michel." Opening Sept. 23 at La Galerie du 19M, Chanel’s craftsmanship hub in northern Paris, the display runs until Dec. 13. The showcase focuses equally on final designs and the ancient tools and techniques at the heart of the craft. Curated by artistic director Priscilla Royer and Palais Galliera museum director Emilie Hammen, the exhibition features carved linden tree trunks, a selection of 4,000 wooden hat blocks from the archives, and specially commissioned artworks. The workshop notes that it is currently witnessing a hat revival, moving away from short-brimmed trends toward dramatic and imposing statement hats that offer room for experimentation. The exhibition space also includes a replica of an early 20th-century milliner’s shop alongside weekly filmmaking workshops hosted by Michel Gondry's studio.

articles.originalTitle: 6 artists to watch at the Lyon Biennale 2026 - Art Basel
articles.title: The 18th Lyon Biennale Explores Exchange and Transition Under Curator Catherine Nichols
articles.excerpt: Curated by Catherine Nichols, the 18th Lyon Biennale brings together 118 artists from around the world across several key venues from September through December 2026.
articles.content: Founded in 1991, the Lyon Biennale returns in September for its 18th edition across several key venues in the city. Curated by Australian writer and art historian Catherine Nichols, the ambitious program brings together 118 artists from around the world. Titled To Pass from One Dream to Another and inspired by Lyon's traboules, the biennale examines physical transitions between spaces and historical layers. Drawing on Robert Filliou's principles of poetic economy, Nichols organizes the event around three distinct layers: the existential at macLYON, the relational at the Musée des Tissus, and the industrial at Les Grandes Locos. The edition features a constellation of artists rarely shown in France, alongside a particularly strong presence from the Oceanian scene. Showcasing works by practitioners such as Akwasi Bediako Afrane, Hana Miletić, Serwah Attafuah, Luke Willis Thompson, Angela Goh, and Minh Lan Tran, the 18th Lyon Biennale runs from September 19 to December 13, 2026.

articles.originalTitle: Biennale Cinema 2026 | Official awards of the 83rd Venice International Film Festival - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: Winners of the 83rd Venice International Film Festival Announced
articles.excerpt: The international juries of the 83rd Venice International Film Festival announced their awards during the ceremony. The Golden Lion for Best Film was awarded to Kvinde Ukendt, directed by May el-Toukhy.
articles.content: The juries of the 83rd Venice International Film Festival have announced their official awards following screenings in various competitive sections. The main competition jury, chaired by Maggie Gyllenhaal, awarded the Golden Lion for Best Film to Kvinde Ukendt, directed by May el-Toukhy across Denmark, Sweden, and Latvia. The Silver Lion Grand Jury Prize went to Possible Love by Lee Chang-dong, while Ilya Khrzhanovsky received the Silver Lion for Best Director for Dau. The Coppa Volpi for Best Actress was awarded to Mathilde Arcel for her role in Kvinde Ukendt, and the Coppa Volpi for Best Actor was presented to John Malkovich for Wild Horse Nine. The screenplay award was given to Stéphane Brizé, Coralie Amédéo, and Olivier Gorce for Un Bon Petit Soldat. In the Orizzonti section, the top prize went to Diane in the Loop by Ann Sirot and Raphaël Balboni. The Luigi De Laurentiis Venice Award for a Debut Film was granted to House of the Wind by Auguste Bernard Kouemo Yanghu. Additionally, the Venice Classics award for best restored film recognized Florestano Vancini's Long Night of 1943.
